record.title: UK proposes a 100 MW indicative threshold and national decision framework for data-centre projects
record.summary: The Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade published an initial proposal for a National Policy Statement (NPS) for data centres in England and opened consultation through 8 January 2027. The draft describes how applications directed into the Nationally Significant Infrastructure Project (NSIP) process would be examined and decided. It says projects with at least 100 MW of rated IT load are likely to be considered nationally significant and suitable for direction under section 35, while allowing case-by-case exceptions. The proposal also sets assessment principles for energy, environment, security and local impacts. It says applicants should arrange annual operator reporting on water use and energy performance, and are expected to demonstrate design PUE of 1.3 or better, with a rationale for less resource-efficient designs. These remain draft expectations; no project decisions, facility compliance or measured effects are demonstrated.
organizations: Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade published an initial proposal for a Data Centre National Policy Statement and opened a public consultation on 28 October 2026, closing 8 January 2027.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The draft says data-centre projects with at least 100 MW of rated IT load are likely to be considered nationally significant and suitable for direction into the NSIP regime under section 35. The Secretary of State would consider projects individually, and exceptional circumstances may permit a direction below that indicative threshold.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The draft sets out proposed assessment principles for consent applications, including energy connections, environmental impacts, security, health and socio-economic effects, with the Secretary of State making decisions following Planning Inspectorate examination.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The draft does not establish a designated National Policy Statement, the outcome of consultation, any individual project direction or consent, construction, compliance, or measured effects on energy, communities, environment or UK compute capacity.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The draft says applicants should arrange for operators to share annual water-use and energy-performance reports with government, and that applicants are expected to demonstrate a design Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of 1.3 or better. A less resource-efficient design requires a stated rationale. These are draft planning expectations, not evidence of operating-facility compliance or measured efficiency.

evidence_gaps.description: The proposal may change following consultation and must proceed through the statutory parliamentary process before designation.
No project-level decisions or results show how the threshold and proposed tests affect data-centre development, energy connections, local impacts or resource use.

brief.importance_rationale: If adopted and applied, a national consent framework and indicative 100 MW threshold could materially affect which large UK data-centre projects can seek NSIP consideration and how energy, environmental, security and community impacts are weighed. The proposal is nationally consequential but remains subject to consultation and parliamentary designation, with no implementation or project outcomes yet shown.
limitations: The document is an initial proposal, not a designated National Policy Statement; consultation closes 8 January 2027.
The 100 MW figure is indicative and applies to rated IT load; the Secretary of State retains case-by-case judgment and may consider exceptional lower-capacity projects.
The publication contains no evidence of individual project approval, construction, policy compliance or realized energy, economic, environmental, security or community effects.

The proposed PUE expectation and annual water/energy reporting arrangements remain draft planning expectations; no facility compliance, measured operational values or AI-workload-normalized efficiency is established.

technical.claimed_result: The government proposes a national decision framework for data-centre projects directed into the NSIP consenting regime, including an indicative 100 MW rated IT load threshold, an expected design PUE of 1.3 or better for applicants and annual operator water-use and energy-performance reporting.
technical.demonstrated_result: The department published the initial proposal and consultation. No final designation or project-level decision is demonstrated.
technical.mechanism: The draft NPS would guide Planning Inspectorate examination and Secretary of State decisions on data-centre consent applications entering the NSIP regime. Section 35 directions remain case-specific, with 100 MW rated IT load presented as an indicative level likely to be nationally significant and exceptions possible. It also proposes that applicants provide for annual water-use and energy-performance reports and demonstrate design PUE of 1.3 or better, or explain a less resource-efficient design.
technical.regime: Proposed planning framework for data-centre development consent in England; consultation published 28 October 2026 and open until 8 January 2027. PUE/reporting provisions are draft application expectations, not evidence of operating performance.
technical.reproducibility: Not applicable to publication of a policy proposal. Implementation and effects require later statutory records and project-level outcome evidence.
technical.strongest_baseline: The draft describes the proposed process and criteria but provides no project-level baseline for consent timelines, capacity built, energy or water use, local effects or compliance.

brief.title: UK proposes a 100 MW indicative threshold and national decision framework for data-centre projects
brief.why_it_matters: A dedicated planning framework could shape how large data-centre projects in England seek nationally significant consent and how their energy, environmental and community impacts are assessed. The proposed PUE expectation and annual water/energy reporting could improve future observability, but neither measures useful AI output or establishes operating outcomes. The 100 MW threshold is indicative, and the draft remains open to consultation; implementation and project effects are not yet established.
